Yes, the demand was too high on 16 June 2025. The plant exceeded its contract capacity of 1250.0 kW during two 15-minute intervals:

*   **08:00**: 1307.1 kW [data: get_demand]
*   **08:15**: 1324.4 kW (the daily peak) [data: get_demand]

The peak demand reached a contract ratio of 1.06 [data: get_demand].

Reflow ovens must be switched off rather than left in standby because a standby oven draws 36% of its 70 kW rating (25.2 kW), which is the largest single source of idle energy over the weekend [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-02_weekend_shutdown.md#SOP-02 Weekend Shutdown > Why reflow ovens must be OFF, not standby].

In incident S5 (2025-10-17 to 2025-10-20), reflow oven RF-02 was left in standby all weekend, resulting in an excess energy consumption of approximately 1,210 kWh [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-02_weekend_shutdown.md#SOP-02 Weekend Shutdown > Why reflow ovens must be OFF, not standby].
